main_diagnosis: The X2 parameter slot (params[:,7] and params[:,9]) is entirely unused, wasting available model capacity at a time when neg_avg_log_marginal_NLE is high (24.2). A single M-current is insufficient to jointly match resting potential mean/SD, stimulation-period voltage distribution moments (variance, skewness, kurtosis), and spike count — a second sub-threshold mechanism is needed. Additionally, tau_M is hard-coded to 100 ms with no ability to adapt, creating a rigid kinetic assumption that may systematically mis-match inter-spike intervals across stimulus intensities.

issues.description: The X2 slot (params[:,7] = gbar_X2, params[:,9] = param_j) is declared but never instantiated into any channel. This leaves two inferred parameters idle while the model fails to match voltage distribution moments (variance, skewness, kurtosis) and resting-potential statistics. A persistent sodium current (INaP) — a slow, non-inactivating, sub-threshold Na+ channel — is a canonical fit here: it depolarises the resting potential slightly, lowers spike threshold, and shapes the subthreshold voltage distribution without producing bursting. Steady-state: m_p_inf = 1/(1+exp(-(V+55)/4)), no inactivation gate, fixed fast kinetics (tau_p ~ 1 ms or treat as instantaneous). Reversal = E_Na = 53 mV.
issues.location: forward() — after gbar_M / E_M parameter unpacking, before time-integration loop
issues.suggestion: Activate the X2 slot as a persistent sodium current: `gbar_NaP = params[:,7].float()` and use `params[:,9].float()` for its half-activation voltage `Vh_NaP` (negate internally so the prior range maps to ~[-65, 0] mV). Inside the loop add: `m_p = 1/(1+Exp(-(V_prev - Vh_NaP)/4.0))`, `I_NaP = gbar_NaP * m_p * (V_prev - E_Na)`. Include `gbar_NaP * m_p` in tau_V_inv and `gbar_NaP * m_p * E_Na` in the V_inf numerator. This leverages both free inferred parameters and directly targets the resting-potential and subthreshold-moment discrepancies without adding bursting dynamics.

issues.description: tau_M is fixed at 100 ms with no inferred flexibility. Wang (1998) reports tau_M in the range 20–300 ms depending on neuron type and voltage. Locking it to 100 ms means the model cannot adapt M-current kinetics to match the actual inter-spike interval regularity or adaptation timescale of the target recordings. This rigidity propagates into errors in spike count, mean stimulation voltage, and higher-order moments across multiple stimulus conditions. Since X2 conductance param (params[:,7]) will now be used for INaP, the M-current time-constant could be rephrased as a scaled version of an existing slot, OR tau_M can be given a data-driven fixed value derived from the target ISI (e.g., 50 ms for faster adaptation) without violating the 2-parameter-per-channel rule.
issues.location: forward() — `tau_M = 100.0` scalar declaration and `Exp(torch.full_like(p_ss, -tstep / tau_M))` in loop
issues.suggestion: Replace the hard-coded `tau_M = 100.0` with a smaller default (e.g., `tau_M = 50.0`) which is more consistent with tonic-spiking adaptation cells and reduces systematic over-smoothing of the M-gate. Alternatively, make tau_M voltage-dependent using a simple empirical form: `tau_M_v = tau_M / (3.3 * (Exp((V_prev+35)/20) + Exp(-(V_prev+35)/20)))` with `tau_M = 100.0` as the base scalar — this is the standard Wang (1998) formulation and improves ISI regularity without adding a free parameter.
